meta.dataset: AMI Meeting Corpus (CC BY 4.0): 1000 clips of 5–15 s from 73 meetings (600 cut from the headset mix, 400 from a far-field table microphone) with the corpus's human word-level transcripts

models.label: Whisper large-v3
models.detail: Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3 @ edaa852 (CTranslate2, float16) via faster-whisper 1.2.1; language=en, beam 5, temperature 0 without fallback, no VAD filter, no previous-text conditioning, library-default no-speech/log-prob thresholds, 30 s window (each clip is one window)

models.label: Whisper small
models.detail: Systran/faster-whisper-small @ 536b066 (CTranslate2, float16) via faster-whisper 1.2.1; language=en, beam 5, temperature 0 without fallback, no VAD filter, no previous-text conditioning, library-default no-speech/log-prob thresholds, 30 s window (each clip is one window)

models.label: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
models.detail: nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 @ 541d1f9 (fp32, transformers 5.24.1); greedy TDT decoding; multilingual checkpoint, no language forcing

models.label: wav2vec 2.0 large (CTC)
models.detail: facebook/wav2vec2-large-960h-lv60-self @ 54074b1 (fp32, transformers 5.24.1); greedy CTC decoding, no language model; fine-tuned on LibriSpeech 960 h only (read audiobooks)

models.label: Moonshine base
models.detail: moonshine-ai/moonshine-base @ 7a73d8d (fp32, transformers 5.24.1); greedy decoding, max 6.5 tokens per second of audio (the model card's hallucination-loop guard)

meta.metric: WER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference words, after Whisper's English text normalizer (plus a small spelling-variant map) is applied identically to reference and hypothesis, so fillers (uh, um, mm), laughter and unfinished word fragments are not scored; aggregates are corpus-level (total errors / total reference words), not means of per-clip WER; with overlapping speech the reference orders every speaker's words by start time, which penalises models that transcribe speakers one after the other (summary.overlap_convention shows the best-of-orderings variant)
meta.input: Every model is fed the clip's 16 kHz mono PCM exactly as cut from the recording: no loudness normalization, no voice-activity detection. Far-field recordings are much quieter than the headset mix. Parakeet and wav2vec 2.0 normalize the level inside their feature extractors; Whisper's log-mel front end depends on it, and a check on every 5th clip (checks/level_sensitivity.py) found far-field WER about 3 points lower with normalized audio and headset WER unchanged; Moonshine's front end does not normalize either, but normalizing changed its overall WER by 0.3 point on all 1,000 clips
meta.normalization: Whisper's EnglishTextNormalizer (lower case, punctuation and bracketed text removed, contractions expanded, number words to digits, British to American spelling, the fillers hmm/mm/mhm/mmm/uh/um removed), applied identically to reference and hypothesis, plus: acronyms written with underscores or dots, and a closed list of spelled-out ones, are joined (T_V_, T.V., 'T V' -> tv); ok/'kay -> okay, alright -> all right, e mail -> email; laughter written as words (ha ha) and tokens with no letter or digit are dropped; a bare 'oh' stays 'oh' (the normalizer prints it as the digit 0). Not unified, so they count as errors: compound spellings (touch screen / touchscreen) and different ways of writing money and decimals
meta.uncertainty: ci95 and 'within sampling noise' come from a bootstrap that resamples whole meeting series (the same participants in the same room; 32 series in this sample) 2,000 times with a fixed seed, because clips from one series are not independent; 'significant' means the 95 % interval of the difference between two groups excludes zero

tags.noise: estimated speech-to-background SNR: mean power of annotated-speech frames vs the median power of the meeting's frames far from any annotated sound, per microphone; low >= 20 dB, mid 10-20 dB, high < 10 dB. In this sample every high-noise clip is a far-field clip and every other clip is headset mix, so noise and microphone distance cannot be separated; the references were transcribed from close-talk headsets, so some far-field words are barely audible in the room microphone
tags.overlap: overlap_ratio = share of speech time with two or more speakers at once (annotations); overlap = ratio >= 0.1
tags.speed: wpm = reference words per minute of speaking time; slow < 145, fast > 200 (dataset quartiles)
tags.accent: AMI's recorded native language of each speaker: non-native when at least half the clip's words come from non-native-English speakers (sampled clips are >= 90 % one or the other). Not a perceptual accent rating
tags.conditions: noisy = high noise (far-field microphone, SNR < 10 dB); overlapping = overlap flag; accented = non-native; clean = none of these. summary.by_condition counts a clip only when that is its ONLY condition; summary.by_condition_any counts every clip carrying the condition

meta.sampling: balanced design: each of noisy / overlapping / accented is on 40 % of clips, pairwise independent, with the single-condition cells enlarged; windows start and end in silences so no word is cut. The sample is stratified on purpose, so its overall WER describes this sample, not AMI as a whole. It is not balanced on recording site: 78% of the native-English clips come from Edinburgh scenario meetings and 79% of the non-native clips from Idiap scenario meetings, and the sites differ in difficulty (Whisper large-v3 on clean clips: 13.3% in Edinburgh scenario meetings, 6.8% in Idiap scenario meetings), so each finding compares groups within one site and summary.by_condition_by_site repeats the condition table per site

findings.title: Overlapping speech
findings.stat: Whisper large-v3's word error rate is 39.7% on clips with 30%+ overlapping speech versus 11.2% on clips with no overlapping speech (n = 21 and 84 clips; headset mix, native-English speakers; Edinburgh scenario meetings only).

chart.x_label: Share of clip with overlapping speech

findings.basis: headset mix, native-English speakers; Edinburgh scenario meetings only

findings.title: Distant, noisy audio
findings.stat: Whisper large-v3's word error rate is 29.8% on clips at <5 dB SNR versus 11.8% on clips at 20–30 dB SNR (n = 30 and 44 clips; native-English speakers, no overlapping speech; headset-mix and far-field clips; Edinburgh scenario meetings only).
findings.basis: native-English speakers, no overlapping speech; headset-mix and far-field clips; Edinburgh scenario meetings only

findings.title: Non-native English
findings.stat: Whisper large-v3's word error rate is 12.2% on non-native speakers versus 6.8% on native-English speakers (n = 124 and 56 clips; headset mix, no overlapping speech; Idiap scenario meetings only).
findings.basis: headset mix, no overlapping speech; Idiap scenario meetings only
